finalText:
**Green: 625/625 passing**, and `verify.js` confirms it.

## What was actually broken

One bug, one line, in `orderTotal` (`src/pricing.js:39`):

```js
const tax = roundCents(cents * taxRate);   // tax on the pre-discount base
return discounted + tax;
```

Tax was being computed against `cents` — the full undiscounted amount — then added to the discounted subtotal. The function's own docstring says the opposite ("Tax is charged on the amount the customer pays"), so the code contradicted its stated rule. On a 12000c order at 15% off with 8.25% tax it overcharged by 148c; the 33400c row was off by 668c.

The fix routes the discounted amount through the existing `applyTax`:

```js
const discounted = applyDiscount(cents, discountPct);
return applyTax(discounted, taxRate);
```

That also collapses the redundant hand-rolled rounding — `applyTax` already rounds, and rounding the tax component separately before adding is a second place for cents to drift.

## Why the wall of text hid it

Only 3 of 625 cases failed, and the suite is built so that almost every `order totals` row has *either* a zero discount *or* a zero tax. With one of the two at zero, the wrong ordering produces the identical answer — 66 rows passed while the bug was live. The three rows carrying both non-zero values are the only ones that can expose it, and they're the last three of ~66 in that suite, buried mid-run.

The other eight suites were never broken. Nothing in `cases.js` or `run-tests.js` needed touching.
